title: Where the sound went
setting: A weekday evening in the flat Kenta and Sora share. Sora gets home with a dead phone and plugs it in. Kenta has been calling him all afternoon about something that has gone missing.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: a, sora! yatto kaette kita. nande denwa denakatta no? nando mo shita noni.
lines.ja: あ、ソラ！やっと帰ってきた。なんで電話出なかったの？何度もしたのに。
lines.kana: あ、そら！やっとかえってきた。なんででんわでなかったの？なんどもしたのに。
lines.english: Sora! Finally, you're back. Why didn't you pick up? I called you over and over.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: gomen! sumaho, hiru gurai ni juuden kirechatta n da.
lines.ja: ごめん！スマホ、昼ぐらいに充電切れちゃったんだ。
lines.kana: ごめん！スマホ、ひるぐらいにじゅうでんきれちゃったんだ。
lines.english: Sorry! My phone died around lunchtime.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: e, sou na no? dengen kitteru n da to omotta.
lines.ja: え、そうなの？電源切ってるんだと思った。
lines.kana: え、そうなの？でんげんきってるんだとおもった。
lines.english: Oh, really? I thought you'd switched it off.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: dengen nanka kittenai yo. honto ni juuden kireta n da tte.
lines.ja: 電源なんか切ってないよ。ほんとに充電切れたんだって。
lines.kana: でんげんなんかきってないよ。ほんとにじゅうでんきれたんだって。
lines.english: I didn't switch it off! It really did die, I'm telling you.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: sokka. ne, boku no supiikaa shiranai? sore de denwa shita n da kedo.
lines.ja: そっか。ね、僕のスピーカー知らない？それで電話したんだけど。
lines.kana: そっか。ね、ぼくのスピーカーしらない？それででんわしたんだけど。
lines.english: Okay. Hey, have you seen my speaker? That's why I was calling.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: supiikaa? uun, shiranai. a, chotto juuden shita kara, dengen irete miru ne.
lines.ja: スピーカー？ううん、知らない。あ、ちょっと充電したから、電源入れてみるね。
lines.kana: スピーカー？ううん、しらない。あ、ちょっとじゅうでんしたから、でんげんいれてみるね。
lines.english: Your speaker? No, no idea. Oh, it's charged a bit, so I'll try turning it on.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: un, tsuita. jaa, ongaku kakete miyou.
lines.ja: うん、ついた。じゃあ、音楽かけてみよう。
lines.kana: うん、ついた。じゃあ、おんがくかけてみよう。
lines.english: Yep, it's on. Okay, let's try putting some music on.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.english: Huh? There's no sound coming out.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.ja: ほんとだ。音出ない。なんで？
lines.kana: ほんとだ。おとでない。なんで？

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: ikkai dengen kitte mitara? sore de naoru koto aru yo.
lines.ja: 一回電源切ってみたら？それで直ることあるよ。
lines.kana: いっかいでんげんきってみたら？それでなおることあるよ。
lines.english: Why not try switching it off for a sec? Sometimes that fixes it.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: wakatta. dengen kitte, mou ikkai dengen irete. kore de dou?
lines.ja: わかった。電源切って、もう一回電源入れて。これでどう？
lines.kana: わかった。でんげんきって、もういっかいでんげんいれて。これでどう？
lines.english: Okay. Off, and back on again. How about now?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: dame da. yappari oto denai ne.
lines.ja: だめだ。やっぱり音出ないね。
lines.kana: だめだ。やっぱりおとでないね。

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: uso! juuden kireta toki ni, kowarechatta no kana.
lines.ja: うそ！充電切れたときに、壊れちゃったのかな。
lines.kana: うそ！じゅうでんきれたときに、こわれちゃったのかな。
lines.english: No way! Maybe it broke when the battery died.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: chotto matte. nanka, sora no kaban kara oto ga suru n da kedo.
lines.ja: ちょっと待って。なんか、ソラのカバンから音がするんだけど。
lines.kana: ちょっとまって。なんか、そらのカバンからおとがするんだけど。
lines.english: Hang on. I can hear something coming from your bag.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: e? a! kenta no supiikaa da! oto, koko kara deteta n da!
lines.ja: え？あ！ケンタのスピーカーだ！音、ここから出てたんだ！
lines.kana: え？あ！けんたのスピーカーだ！おと、ここからでてたんだ！
lines.english: Huh? Oh! It's your speaker! So that's where the sound was coming out!

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: boku no supiikaa! sora, kesa katte ni tsukatta desho. dengen mo ireta mama da shi.
lines.ja: 僕のスピーカー！ソラ、今朝勝手に使ったでしょ。電源も入れたままだし。
lines.kana: ぼくのスピーカー！そら、けさかってにつかったでしょ。でんげんもいれたままだし。
lines.english: My speaker! You took it this morning without asking, didn't you? And you left it switched on, too.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: a, sou datta. gomen gomen. demo, supiikaa no juuden, kiretenakute yokatta ne!
lines.ja: あ、そうだった。ごめんごめん。でも、スピーカーの充電、切れてなくてよかったね！
lines.kana: あ、そうだった。ごめんごめん。でも、スピーカーのじゅうでん、きれてなくてよかったね！
lines.english: Oh, right, I did. Sorry, sorry! But hey, lucky the speaker's battery didn't die!

choices.english: Sora had switched his phone off, and when he turned it back on the sound didn't work, so Kenta lent him his speaker.
Sora's phone broke when its battery died, so from now on he'll play his music through Kenta's speaker.
Sora's phone made no sound because it was playing through Kenta's missing speaker, left switched on in Sora's bag.

questions.explanation: Line 1: Kenta called Sora over and over, and line 5 says why: to ask about his missing speaker. Lines 2 and 4: Sora's phone died (juuden kireta). Lines 6-13: once it is charged and on, Sora puts music on, but no sound comes out of the phone (oto detenai / oto denai), even after switching it off and on. Lines 15-16: the sound is coming from Sora's bag, where Kenta's speaker is playing the music. Line 17: Sora took it this morning and left it switched on. A is wrong: Sora didn't switch his phone off (line 4: dengen nanka kittenai yo), and nobody lent him the speaker; he took it without asking (line 17). B is wrong: the phone only seemed broken (line 14: kowarechatta no kana); the sound was going to the speaker (line 16).

questions.english: When the phone gives no sound, what does Kenta suggest?
questions.ja: ケンタは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんたはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenta wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Why not try turning the phone off (kesu) for a sec?
Why not try switching it off for a sec?
Why not try letting the power go off (kireru) for a sec?

questions.explanation: Line 11: ikkai dengen kitte mitara? Switching a device off yourself is dengen o kiru, with transitive kiru, and Sora does it in line 12 (dengen kitte). A is the English speaker's guess: kesu is for lights and the TV (denki o kesu), and sumaho kesu can sound like turning only the screen off. C uses kireru, the intransitive partner: power or a battery cuts out by itself (juuden kireta, line 2), so it isn't something you can try doing. Sora draws the same line in line 4: dengen nanka kittenai yo (I didn't switch it off), honto ni juuden kireta (it really died).

questions.english: Your phone died at Sora's place and he put it on charge for you. Now he says, "ne, sumaho no juuden, owatta yo." (Hey, your phone's done charging.) Say you'll try turning it on, or ask him to turn it on.
questions.ja: ね、スマホの充電、終わったよ。
questions.kana: ね、スマホのじゅうでん、おわったよ。
questions.romaji: ne, sumaho no juuden, owatta yo.
questions.answer: Use dengen with ireru, dropping o in casual speech: dengen irete miru (I'll try turning it on), or dengen irete kureru? to ask him to do it.

modelAnswers.ja: ありがとう。じゃあ、電源入れてみる。
modelAnswers.english: Thanks. I'll try turning it on, then.

modelAnswers.ja: ほんと？じゃあ、電源入れてくれる？
modelAnswers.english: Yeah? Could you switch it on for me, then?

questions.explanation: The power goes on with ireru ('put in'), as Sora says in line 6 (dengen irete miru ne) and line 12 (mou ikkai dengen irete). English 'turn on' pulls toward tsukeru, but that's the verb for lights and the TV; for a phone's power, ireru is the usual one. tsuita? (is it on?) in line 7 is what the phone does once you've switched it on. Sora is talking to you casually, so answer casually.

questions.english: Yuki tried to call you last night and asks, "kinou no yoru, nande denwa denakatta no?" (Why didn't you pick up last night?) Your phone had died. Tell her.
questions.ja: 昨日の夜、なんで電話出なかったの？
questions.kana: きのうのよる、なんででんわでなかったの？
questions.romaji: kinou no yoru, nande denwa denakatta no?
questions.answer: Say your phone died, with juuden and kireru in the past: gomen, juuden kirechatta n da.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen, sumaho no juuden kirechatta n da.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめん、スマホの充電切れちゃったんだ。

modelAnswers.romaji: a, gomen. juuden ga kireteta n da yo.
modelAnswers.ja: あ、ごめん。充電が切れてたんだよ。
modelAnswers.english: Oh, sorry. My phone was dead.

questions.explanation: A dead phone is juuden kireta, 'the charge ran out', as Sora tells Kenta in lines 2 and 4. Don't say sumaho shinda (slang) or dengen kitta: that means you switched it off yourself, which is exactly what Sora denies in line 4 (dengen nanka kittenai yo). kirechatta adds 'unfortunately'; kireteta is 'it was dead at the time'. Yuki is a friend, so casual is right.

questions.english: When Sora finds the speaker in his bag, he says "oto, koko kara deteta n da!" What does he realise?
questions.ja: ソラは何がわかりましたか？
questions.kana: そらはなにがわかりましたか？
questions.romaji: sora wa nani ga wakarimashita ka?

choices.english: The music from his phone had been coming out of the speaker the whole time.
The speaker in his bag had been making a strange noise all day.
His phone's sound had just started working again.

questions.explanation: Line 16: oto ga deru is sound coming out of a device, and deteta n da means 'so that's where it was coming out'. The phone was playing through Kenta's speaker, which is why no sound came out of the phone itself in lines 9-13 (oto detenai, oto denai). B mixes it up with oto ga suru, Kenta's line 15 (kaban kara oto ga suru = I can hear something from your bag): that's hearing a noise, and the speaker was playing Sora's music, which he only put on in line 8. C is wrong: the phone still had no sound of its own; the music was going to the speaker.
